title: Bitcoin proof of work
outcome: Reproduce the relationship between a block header, nonce, hash, and target.
show: Open the Golden Goose verifier. Identify the reported block hash and check the evidence it gives for the header’s embedded target.
concepts: The 80-byte Bitcoin block header includes the version, previous block hash, Merkle root, time, compact target and nonce.
Bitcoin applies SHA-256 twice to the header. The resulting hash, interpreted as an integer in Bitcoin’s convention, must be at or below the target.
A miner can change the nonce and, when necessary, update other permitted candidate fields. A new coinbase extranonce changes the Merkle root. A smaller target is harder to meet.
replicate: Use the toy target of 20. Of hashes 70, 20, 5, and 21, circle every value the rule accepts.
Trace the header fields from the Bitcoin reference and compare the toy rule with the same inequality in the live verifier.
check: Does verifying a public block header earn any Bitcoin?
Header verification checks proof already found. Mining seeks new valid work for a candidate block.
